[1;90mORIGINATING HEXAGRAM NAME AND PRONUNCIATION:

[90m[Traditional Chinese]

  [1;97m未濟（ㄨㄟˋ ㄐㄧˋ）

[90m[Simplified Chinese]

  [1;97m未济（wèi jì）

[90m[English, Wilhelm-Baynes]

  [1;97mWei Chi / Before Completion

[90m[English, James Legge]

  [1;97mLXIV. The Wei Žî Hexagram


[1;90mLINES:
[0m(One moving line)

[90m[Traditional Chinese]

  [0m(Scripture)
  [1;97m初六：濡其尾，吝。

  [0m(Exegesis)
  [1;97m濡其尾，亦不知極也。

[90m[Simplified Chinese]

  [0m(Scripture)
  [1;97m初六：濡其尾，吝。

  [0m(Exegesis)
  [1;97m濡其尾，亦不知极也。

[90m[English, Wilhelm-Baynes]

  [0m(Scripture)
  [1;97mSix at the beginning means:
  He gets his tail in the water.
  Humiliating.

  [0m(Exegesis)
  [1;97mSix at the beginning:
  a) He gets his tail in the water.
  Humiliating.
  b) “He gets his tail in the water.” For he cannot take the end into view.

[90m[English, James Legge]

  [0m(Scripture)
  [1;97m1. The first SIX, divided, shows its subject (like a fox) whose tail gets immersed. There will be occasion for regret.

  [0m(Exegesis)
  [1;97m1. 'His tail gets immersed:'--this is the very height of ignorance.

[1;90mRESULTANT HEXAGRAM NAME AND PRONUNCIATION:

[90m[Traditional Chinese]

  [1;97m睽（ㄎㄨㄟˊ）

[90m[Simplified Chinese]

  [1;97m睽（kuí）

[90m[English, Wilhelm-Baynes]

  [1;97mK’uei / Opposition

[90m[English, James Legge]

  [1;97mXXXVIII. The Khwei Hexagram


[1;90mLINES:
[0m(No moving lines)

[90m[Traditional Chinese]

  [0m(Scripture)
  [1;97m睽：小事吉。

  [0m(Exegesis)
  [1;97m上火下澤，睽；君子以同而異。

[90m[Simplified Chinese]

  [0m(Scripture)
  [1;97m睽：小事吉。

  [0m(Exegesis)
  [1;97m上火下泽，睽；君子以同而异。

[90m[English, Wilhelm-Baynes]

  [0m(Scripture)
  [1;97mOPPOSITION. In small matters, good fortune.

  [0m(Exegesis)
  [1;97mAbove, fire; below, the lake:
  The image of OPPOSITION.
  Thus amid all fellowship
  The superior man retains his individuality.

[90m[English, James Legge]

  [0m(Scripture)
  [1;97mKhwei indicates that, (notwithstanding the condition of things which it denotes), in small matters there will (still) be good success.

  [0m(Exegesis)
  [1;97mXXXVIII. (The trigram representing) fire above, and that for (the waters of) a marsh below, form Khwei. The superior man, in accordance with this, where there is a general agreement, yet admits diversity.
